title: The Many Deaths of a Painting

sentences.en: Barbara Visser was nine years old the first time she saw it.
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉·维瑟第一次见到它时才九岁。

sentences.en: She was on a school field trip to the Städelik Art Museum in the center of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 当时她正随学校去阿姆斯特丹市中心的市立博物馆参观。

sentences.en: One could say it's the heyday of that museum.
sentences.zh: 可以说那是那座博物馆的全盛时期。

sentences.en: They were really at the forefront of modern and contemporary art.
sentences.zh: 他们确实走在现代艺术和当代艺术的最前沿。

sentences.en: The Städelik was built to impress.
sentences.zh: 市立博物馆的建筑设计旨在给人留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: There was a huge stairway leading up to the light, in a way, a bit biblical.
sentences.zh: 那里有一条通往光亮处的巨大楼梯，某种程度上，带有一点圣经色彩。

sentences.en: A stairway not to heaven, but almost to heaven, to the Hall of Honours.
sentences.zh: 那不是通往天堂的阶梯，但几乎是了，通往荣誉大厅。

sentences.en: The Hall of Honours displayed some of the museum's finest paintings,
sentences.zh: 荣誉大厅陈列着博物馆最精美的一些画作，

sentences.en: but one in particular dominated the room.
sentences.zh: 但其中一幅画尤为引人注目，占据了整个房间。

sentences.en: The tour guide led Barbara and her class over.
sentences.zh: 导游带着芭芭拉和她的同学们走了过去。

sentences.en: And this painting, it struck me like lightning.
sentences.zh: 而这幅画，像闪电一样击中了我。

sentences.en: And not in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 而且不是什么好的感觉。

sentences.en: What she saw was a massive canvas, nearly 18 feet wide and 8 feet tall.
sentences.zh: 她看到的是一幅巨大的画布，宽近18英尺，高8英尺。

sentences.en: On the left side, a small strip of blue.
On the right, a small strip of yellow.
But the rest of the surface was painted entirely red.
sentences.zh: 但其余的表面完全涂成了红色。

sentences.en: And it kind of annoyed me.
I really, I didn't know what to look at, where to stare, what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 我真的，我不知道该看哪里，该盯着哪里，该拿它怎么办。

sentences.en: And the only thing that the guide shared with us was the title.
sentences.zh: 而导游告诉我们的唯一信息就是它的标题。

sentences.en: And the title is A Question.
Who's Afraid of Red, Yellow and Blue?
I ran out of the museum.
I sat on the steps and was determined not to go in again.
sentences.zh: 我坐在台阶上，下定决心再也不进去了。

sentences.en: The full title of the painting Barbara saw that day is Who's Afraid of Red, Yellow and Blue 3?
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉那天看到的画，全名是《谁害怕红、黄、蓝 3？》

sentences.en: By the American post-war artist Barnett Newman.
sentences.zh: 作者是美国战后艺术家巴尼特·纽曼。

sentences.en: Producer John Fasile brings us this tale from the galleries of Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 制片人约翰·法西尔为我们带来了这个发生在阿姆斯特丹画廊里的故事。

sentences.en: Usually, you walk into a museum, you see a painting, you think about it for a moment, maybe feel something, and walk away.
sentences.zh: 通常，你走进博物馆，看到一幅画，思考片刻，也许会有所感触，然后走开。

sentences.en: This was a painting that would produce such strong reactions in people that they did more than just think about it.
sentences.zh: 这幅画能在人们心中激起如此强烈的反应，以至于他们不仅仅是思考它。

sentences.en: In the end, Barbara got off easy.
She only struggled with the painting her entire life and made a feature-length documentary about it.
sentences.zh: 她只是终其一生都在与这幅画较劲，并为此制作了一部专题纪录片。

sentences.en: It's called The End of Fear, and it inspired this story.
sentences.zh: 片名叫《恐惧的终结》，它启发了这个故事。

sentences.en: And this story is about a reaction the painting received that was so intense, so violent.
sentences.zh: 而这个故事讲述的是这幅画所收到的一种反应，它是如此强烈，如此暴力。

sentences.en: It set off a chain of events that shook the art world to its core.
sentences.zh: 它引发了一连串事件，震撼了整个艺术界。

sentences.en: It wasn't easy art, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少可以说，这不是容易理解的艺术。
但首先，为什么是这幅画？

sentences.en: The problem of the subject became very clear to me as the crucial thing in painting.
sentences.zh: 主题的问题对我来说变得非常清晰，它是绘画中的关键所在。

sentences.en: Barnett Newman was a late bloomer, a substitute art teacher turned art critic turned artiSt.
sentences.zh: 巴尼特·纽曼是大器晚成的人，他当过代课美术老师，后来成了艺术评论家，最后成为艺术家。

sentences.en: He didn't have his first solo show until he was almost 45.
sentences.zh: 直到快45岁时，他才举办了第一次个展。

sentences.en: He was this portly Jewish guy with a big friendly mustache who wore a lot of bow ties and went by the nickname Barney.
sentences.zh: 他是个胖乎乎的犹太人，留着浓密友好的胡子，经常打领结，绰号叫巴尼。

sentences.en: And he quickly became the de facto spokesman for a new art movement called Abstract Expressionism.
sentences.zh: 他很快成为了一个名为“抽象表现主义”的新艺术运动的实际代言人。

sentences.en: A painter is a kind of choreographer of space.
sentences.zh: 画家是一种空间的编舞者。

sentences.en: He creates kind of a dance of elements, of forMs.
sentences.zh: 他创造了一种元素、形式的舞蹈。

sentences.en: Abstract Expressionism came out of New York after World War II.
sentences.zh: 抽象表现主义兴起于二战后的纽约。

sentences.en: The movement produced painters like Jackson Pollock, Mark Rothko, and Helen Frankenthaler.
sentences.zh: 这场运动涌现了杰克逊·波洛克、马克·罗斯科和海伦·弗兰肯塔勒等画家。

sentences.en: Artists known for big canvases full of wild colors, shapes, and splashes of paint.
sentences.zh: 这些艺术家以充满狂野色彩、形状和泼溅颜料的巨幅画布而闻名。

sentences.en: Like many Abstract Expressionist artists, Newman struggled with what to paint in the aftermath of the war.
sentences.zh: 像许多抽象表现主义艺术家一样，纽曼在战后也在思考该画些什么。

sentences.en: I felt the issue in those years was, what can a painter do?
sentences.zh: 我觉得那些年里的问题是，画家能做什么？

sentences.en: After all, what could you paint after the Holocaust?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，大屠杀之后还能画什么？

sentences.en: What are we going to paint?
For Newman, answering this question required ignoring all of art history and starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 对纽曼来说，回答这个问题需要抛弃所有的艺术史，从零开始。

sentences.en: He began making large paintings, big even by Abstract Expressionist standards,
sentences.zh: 他开始创作大幅画作，即使以抽象表现主义的标准来看也很大，

sentences.en: often filling the entire wall of a gallery.
sentences.zh: 经常填满画廊的整面墙。

sentences.en: In the end, size doesn't count.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，尺寸并不重要。

sentences.en: These paintings were physically big, and they felt even bigger.
sentences.zh: 这些画在物理上很大，而且感觉更大。

sentences.en: They featured very few colors, usually one solid hue, broken up by a few vertical stripes.
sentences.zh: 它们使用的颜色很少，通常是一种纯色，被几条垂直的条纹打破。

sentences.en: But whatever you do, don't call them stripes.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，别叫它们条纹。

sentences.en: I did not decide to say to myself, I'm going to paint stripes.
sentences.zh: 我并没有决定对自己说，我要画条纹。

sentences.en: Newman preferred to call them zips.
sentences.zh: 纽曼更喜欢称它们为“拉链”。

sentences.en: I feel that my zip does not divide my painting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的“拉链”并没有分割我的画。

sentences.en: I feel it does the exact opposite.
In 1967, Newman finished what would prove to be one of his largest paintings,
sentences.zh: 1967年，纽曼完成了他最大的一幅画作，

sentences.en: Who's Afraid of Red, Yellow, and Blue, 3.
It was the third in a series.
The title was a reference to Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf,
sentences.zh: 标题参考了《谁害怕弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫》，

sentences.en: a landmark play, later a movie, starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton,
sentences.zh: 这是一部里程碑式的戏剧，后来被改编成电影，由伊丽莎白·泰勒和理查德·伯顿主演，

sentences.en: about a relationship full of miscommunication,
sentences.zh: 讲述了一段充满误解的关系，

sentences.en: In a sense, this big red painting with a slender zip of blue on the left
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这幅巨大的红色画作，左边有一条细细的蓝色“拉链”，

sentences.en: and a slender zip of yellow on the right was Newman's way of saying,
sentences.zh: 右边有一条细细的黄色“拉链”，是纽曼表达的方式，

sentences.en: this is what a painting can do.
But what was the painting doing exactly?
sentences.zh: 但这幅画到底在做什么？

sentences.en: Barbara Visser says that when the Stadelic Museum acquired Who's Afraid of Red,
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉·维瑟说，当市立博物馆在1969年购入《谁害怕红、

sentences.zh: 其实，我们用“厌恶”这个词吧。

sentences.en: to say how much they hated this painting.
sentences.zh: 来表达他们有多讨厌这幅画。

sentences.en: The painting evoked a common complaint about abstract art,
sentences.zh: 这幅画引发了人们对抽象艺术的一个普遍抱怨，

sentences.en: which is to throw your hands up and say,
I paid to see art, damn it, not red paint on a canvas.
sentences.zh: 该死，我花钱是来看艺术的，不是看画布上的红油漆。

sentences.en: There was one woman who expressed that it really nauseated her
sentences.zh: 有一位女士表示，它真的让她感到恶心，

sentences.en: and it really, literally made her sick.
sentences.zh: 真的，字面意义上让她感到不适。

sentences.en: She felt it would better be hung out of sight,
sentences.zh: 她觉得最好把它挂在看不见的地方，

sentences.en: somewhere in the coat, the coat check.

La Grande Parade is precies wat hij zegt te zijn.
The purpose of which was to raise exactly this question

sentences.en: of what a painting is or isn't.

Yellow, and Blue, 3 were taken to a whole new level.
sentences.zh: 黄、蓝 3》的负面评价被提升到了一个全新的高度。

sentences.zh: 当时，芭芭拉正在艺术学校读书。

sentences.en: Somehow in the corridors of the school,
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，在学校的走廊里，

I was on my way to the Stadelic Museum for a meeting.
sentences.zh: 我当时正要去市立博物馆开会。

sentences.zh: 佩特拉·滕卡塔，一位艺术家兼教育家，

sentences.zh: 那天下午走进了市立博物馆。

And then I came upon that room,

sentences.zh: 一名工作人员站在角落里，吓得动弹不得。

sentences.en: The painting had just been attacked.
And the man who did it sat on the bench.
sentences.zh: 而那个肇事者坐在长椅上。

sentences.en: The tall, brown-haired man, sitting quietly on the bench,
sentences.zh: 那个高个子、棕色头发的男人，安静地坐在长椅上，

sentences.zh: 把它全部垂直切开，还有长长的、长长的水平切口。

sentences.en: The canvas had lost its tension and sagged,
sentences.zh: 画布失去了张力，下垂了，

sentences.zh: 把切口变成了歪斜的笑脸，

I remember I got a call,

that his lawyer made in his defense
